subject: Post-demo: country locks, failover matrix & data handling follow-ups
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@medconnect.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@medconnect.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: country locks, failover matrix & data handling follow-ups

Hi Alyssa / Jorge — thanks again for the call earlier. Helpful to walk through the integration surface and the regulatory constraints for MedConnect. Quick recap and a handful of specific follow-ups so we can size the work and lock the next steps. Attaching a short SOC 2 summary for background.

Recap (brief):
- Primary requirement: keep patient PII and conversation transcripts stored and processed in US-only region for the pilot.
- Secondary: warm standby in another US availability zone (not cross-border) for failover.
- Audit requirement: long-term audit logs retained separately for 7 years.

Questions / asks (please confirm the bullets you care about and any details we missed):
1) PII scope: for clarity, when you say "PII", does MedConnect want all full transcripts treated as PII, or only structured identifiers (SSN, DOB, MRN)? We can support both but the handling differs.
2) Retention windows: you mentioned 30 days for conversational data — can you confirm whether that is from last user activity or last index/update?
3) Logging: are you ok with application-level request/response logs being stored for 30 days and audit logs retained for 7 years (immutable store)?
4) Pinning: do you require a hard "country lock" that prevents any compute or storage outside US boundaries, or is a "region anchoring" (primary-US, standby-US-only) acceptable?
5) Failover behavior: for warm standby we support manual failover and automated failover. Which level is acceptable for pilot (we recommend manual + runbook)?
6) Compliance artifacts: please confirm which documents you want from us next (full SOC2 report, DPA, encryption specs, or an ops runbook).

Proposed next steps:
- Once you confirm Q1–Q6, I’ll route answers from our solutions + security teams and deliver an ops-runbook + DPA draft.
- Technical workshop to go over pinning and failover matrix (30–45 min).

Availability: I can run the technical workshop next week — are mornings PST / early afternoons PST best?

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (summary, not full report)

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@medconnect.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: country locks, failover matrix & data handling follow-ups

Rafael — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers below and one new ask from our security team.

- PII scope: We treat full conversation transcripts as sensitive PHI when they include identifiers. For the pilot, classify everything as sensitive and then we can scope exceptions.
- Retention: 30 days from last user activity is our baseline for conversation data. Audit logs are a hard 7 years.
- Logging: App-level diagnostic traces can be 30 days; request/response payloads containing PII must be deleted/redacted after 30 days unless preserved in our audit store (separate).
- Pinning: We require a strict US-only residency for the pilot (no cross-border replication). Warm standby must be within US regions only.
- Failover: Manual failover with an ops runbook is preferred for this initial phase.

New ask: Our security team wants a short playbook that describes the failover steps, roles (who executes), and how logs and KV caches are handled during failover. Also need a DPA draft and encryption-at-rest/in-transit confirmation.

If you can send the runbook + DPA draft and propose times for a 45-minute technical workshop, we can coordinate with our infra folks.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Head of Security & Compliance | MedConnect Health
alyssa.turner@medconnect.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: country locks, failover matrix & data handling follow-ups

Team — forwarding Alyssa’s reply. Highlights and proposed approach below. Please treat as FYI + ask for quick inputs so I can respond with specifics and the runbook.

MedConnect asks (summary):
- Strict US-only residency for pilot, warm standby within US only.
- Conversation transcripts treated as sensitive; delete/redact PII-containing payloads after 30 days unless moved to audit store.
- Audit logs retained 7 years immutable.
- Manual failover required; they want an ops playbook and a DPA draft.

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Residency/pinning: Create a US-only tenant for the pilot and enable region anchoring to a primary US AZ with a warm standby in a secondary US AZ. No cross-border replication or cold backups outside US.
2) Data handling: Implement a retention pipeline: conversational store TTL=30d (delete job triggered from last activity timestamp), audit store write-once with 7y retention and WORM-like controls.
3) Logging: Request/response payloads containing PII are redacted before persisting to diagnostic logs; full payloads can be written to the audit store if requested and consented.
4) Failover runbook: Manual failover steps, pre-checks, post-failover validation (traffic smoke tests, KV cache restore notes). I’ll draft a 2‑page runbook.
5) DPA & artifacts: Attach DPA draft and SOC2 summary; security will need encryption spec (we use TLS1.2+ and AES-256 at rest) and key management details (KMS/HSM options).

Questions for you both:
- Karthik: can you confirm implementation constraints for the retention TTL job and whether we can support per-tenant TTL with current infra?
- Monica: can you help draft the runbook skeleton and include explicit roles/permissions (who can trigger failover, who approves)? Also confirm time estimate to produce DPA-ready language with our legal team.

I’ll aim to get the first-pass runbook + DPA draft to Alyssa by Thursday EOD their time if we can lock the language today.

Thanks,
Rafael

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@medconnect.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@medconnect.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: country locks, failover matrix & data handling follow-ups

Alyssa / Jorge — appreciate the quick clarifications. Per our internal review, answers and deliverables below. Attaching: DPA draft (editable), runbook (runbook-region-failover.xlsx), and SOC2 summary. Links to the playbook and DPA are below for ease of review.

Short answers (confirming your bullets):
- Residency: We will provision a dedicated US-only tenant for MedConnect for the pilot. No data or compute will be provisioned in EU/APAC for that tenant. Backups and warm standby will be restricted to US regions only.
- PII scope & retention: We will treat all transcripts as sensitive by default. Conversational data TTL = 30 days from last user activity. Audit store retention = 7 years with append-only controls.
- Logging: Application diagnostic traces retained 30 days; PII-containing payloads are redacted in diagnostic logs. If MedConnect elects to persist full payloads, those will be written to the audit store with the 7-year retention and access controls.
- Failover: We recommend manual failover for the pilot. The attached runbook lists the exact steps, roles (Operator, Technical Approver, Customer Contact), and acceptance checks.
- Encryption: In transit: TLS1.2+ (we recommend TLS1.3 where available). At rest: AES-256 with customer KMS option (if you want separate key control we can enable a dedicated key).

Deliverables attached / links:
- SOC2_summary.pdf (attached)
- runbook-region-failover.xlsx (attached) — short playbook with roles and checklists
- DPA_MedConnect_signed-draft.pdf (attached) — DPA draft for review and countersignature. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/to/DPA-MedConnect
- Playbook folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-medconnect-playbook

Next steps:
1) Please confirm any edits to the runbook/DPA by EOD Friday and we’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature.
2) Technical workshop: propose Thurs 21 May 2026, 10:00–10:45 AM PST or Fri 22 May 2026, 8:00–8:45 AM PST. Which works for your infra/security folks?
3) If you prefer, we can include a brief infra-level session on retention TTL implementation and audit-store access control during the workshop.

If anything here needs to be harder-specified (e.g., a particular KMS vendor or exact WORM storage product), list it and we’ll get the security engineering owner to join.

Best — looking forward to the workshop.

Rafael Mendes
